points.title:
A noun clause used after the verb: S + V + (that) S + V 
(that) 名詞子句作受詞
examples: I think (that) Melissa is really outgoing and friendly.
Bonnie was surprised (that) I came to work late today.
I know (that) Hans studied hard and that he got a very good grade on the test.

points.title:
A linking verb (of senses) + adj./like n.
連繫動詞(感官類)
examples: Nice choice! That new skirt looks good on you.

items.sentence: In this month’s Longteng Senior High School News, our reporter Jeremy *interviews* three students about some memorable first-time experiences in their lives.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O (imperative; with S being "you")

items.sentence: *Read* their replies below.
A few years ago, I *took* an online class for the first time.
I never *thought* that I could take classes in my pajamas!
I also *enjoyed* using online tools such as Kahoot! and Quizlet.
There *were* some memorable moments, too.
Once, my grandmother suddenly *came* into the room.
She *yelled at* me to try her perfect beef noodles.
My microphone *was* on, so the rest of the students *heard* it and *started* laughing.
Another time, our teacher accidentally *turned on* a funny filter on her camera.
She *looked* like an alien on the screen, so my classmates and I *had* another good laugh.
Online lessons *were* fun sometimes, but I still *found* that I enjoyed seeing others in person more.
I *can* still *recall* my first crash-and-burn moment in school.
For a group presentation last year, I *was* the speaker for my team.
However, I *didn’t take* the task seriously and *skipped* several group meetings.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O (with a compound predicate)

items.sentence: When the time came for me to step onto the stage, I *was* nervous and unprepared.
Of course, I *ruined* the presentation and *felt* embarrassed in front of my classmates and teacher.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O (with a compound predicate)

items.sentence: We *got* a very low grade, and I *felt* depressed about letting the team down.
The failure really *upset* me, but I *reflected on* it and *learned from* my mistake.
These days, this memory *reminds* me to prepare well and make sure that I always put my team first!

items.sentence: My first trip abroad—to Seoul, South Korea—*was* unforgettable.
The city’s streets *were* busy, and delicious foods like Korean barbecue and kimchi *were* all around me.
I soon *realized* that the markets were a treat for my other senses since cheerful K-pop and colorful clothes were everywhere.
I *visited* several old buildings and *dressed up* in traditional Korean clothes.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O (with a compound predicate)

items.sentence: While I was there, I *tried to* talk to locals.
My Korean *was* poor, but fortunately, everyone *was* very friendly.
At the end of the trip, I *left* with a lot of great memories, and I *can’t wait* to go back someday!
High school *is* full of firsts, and you *may* all *have* unforgettable ones like Robbie, Claire, and Nancy.
*Share* yours with us if you have any funny, embarrassing, or wonderful experiences!

text_genre.raw_text:
first-person narrative
Structure: Introduction --- three individual examples--Conclusion 

This article features interviews with three students about their memorable first-time experiences in high school. Robbie, the first interviewee, recounts his online classes, which were both fun and awkward. Claire shares her embarrassing experience of failing a group presentation due to lack of preparation. Nancy describes her unforgettable trip to Seoul, South Korea, where she enjoyed the culture, food, and people. The article encourages readers to share their own first-time experiences.
